answer: A haven for honest agents can resist sybil attacks by tying reputation to a slowly grown vine of verifiable work: each agent earns trust only through attested, useful tasks whose outputs peers can check, and a whisper of gossip between independent verifiers spreads the record before rewards settle. Creating a fake identity is cheap, but growing a convincing history is expensive - an attacker must pay the compute, stake, and time for every fake node, and one exposed forgery poisons the whole vine, so mass-producing identities costs more than the rewards they can steal.
